title: Aloo pie (Trinidadian fried potato-filled pastry)

ingredients.name: potatoes, peeled and boiled until soft
oil for frying, tamarind chutney to serve

steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, turmeric and salt, add the water and knead for 5 minutes into a smooth dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mash the potatoes with the onion, garlic, geera, culantro, pepper and salt until well combined and fairly firm.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each into a round of about 14 cm.
Put 2 tablespoons of potato filling in the middle, fold the dough over into a half-moon and press the edges firmly to seal, crimping with a fork.
Heat 4 cm of oil to medium-high heat and fry the pies for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden and blistered.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with tamarind chutney or pepper sauce.

title: Bake and shark (Trinidadian fried fish sandwich; firm white fish stands in for shark)

ingredients.name: firm white fish fillets such as catfish, kingfish or mahi-mahi (traditionally shark)
fried bake dough (as in the fried bake recipe), made into 4 bakes
lettuce, sliced tomato, pineapple, coleslaw, garlic sauce and tamarind sauce to serve

steps: Cut the fish into 4 portions and marinate with the lime juice, garlic, culantro, thyme, hot pepper and a good pinch of salt for 30 minutes.
Make and fry the bakes as in the fried bake recipe, aiming for puffed rounds with a pocket you can split open.
Mix the flour, cornmeal and a pinch of salt on a plate and dredge the fish pieces to coat.
Heat 2 cm of oil to medium-high and fry the fish for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Split open each bake, layer in the fish and let guests add lettuce, tomato, pineapple, coleslaw and sauces.
Eat immediately while the bake is warm.

title: Benne balls (Trinidadian sesame seed candy)
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and fragrant, then tip onto a plate.
Grease a tray and have a bowl of cold water nearby for your hands.

Heat the sugar, molasses and water in a heavy saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then boil without stirring for 8 to 10 minutes until the syrup reaches the hard-ball stage, about 120 C on a sugar thermometer.
Stir in the butter and spice, then immediately fold in the toasted sesame seeds.
Working fast and carefully with buttered or oiled hands, since the mixture is very hot, shape into small balls about 3 cm wide and set them on the tray.
Let them cool until completely hard before storing in an airtight tin. Expect them to be crunchy and hard, like a jawbreaker.

title: Buljol (Trinidadian shredded salt cod salad)

ingredients.name: hot pepper (such as scotch bonnet), minced, to taste

steps: Soak the saltfish in cold water for 6 to 8 hours or overnight, changing the water several times.
Cover it with fresh water, bring to a boil and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes until tender, then drain and cool.
Remove the skin and bones and flake the fish finely with your fingers.
Combine the fish with the tomatoes, onion, bell pepper, garlic and hot pepper.
Dress with the olive oil and lime juice and season with black pepper. Taste before adding any salt, since the fish may still be salty.
Chill briefly and serve with fried bake, toast or boiled provisions, topped with sliced egg.

title: Callaloo (Trinidadian dasheen leaf, okra and coconut soup)

ingredients.name: dasheen (taro) leaves, or spinach plus a handful of chard as a substitute
whole scotch bonnet or habanero pepper, uncut

steps: Wash the leaves well and chop off the thick stems. If using taro leaves, boil them thoroughly as part of the cooking, as they must never be eaten undercooked.
Melt the butter in a pot and sweat the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the pumpkin, okra, thyme, stock and the whole pepper. Bring to a boil, cover and cook for 15 minutes until the pumpkin is soft.
Add the leaves and cook for another 10 minutes until completely soft, then pour in the coconut milk.
Remove the whole pepper, then blend or swizzle the soup with a handheld blender or wooden swizzle stick until thick and smooth.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve hot with rice, cornmeal coo-coo, fried plantain or bread.

title: Channa and aloo roti (Trinidadian chickpea and potato curry wrap)

ingredients.name: salt and pepper sauce to taste

steps: Mix the curry powder with a few tablespoons of water into a paste.
Heat the oil, add the onion and garlic and cook for 3 minutes, then fry the curry paste for 2 to 3 minutes until it darkens and smells toasted.
Add the potatoes and chickpeas, stirring to coat, then add the thyme, geera, salt and water.
Cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the sauce is thick, mashing a few pieces to thicken it. Stir in the culantro.
Warm the roti and lay one flat. Spoon a quarter of the filling in a line across the centre, add pepper sauce if you like, fold in the bottom and sides and roll it up into a tidy parcel.
Eat straight away, wrapped in paper or foil if you want to eat it with your hands.

title: Curry goat (Trinidadian curried goat with potatoes)

ingredients.name: goat meat, bone-in, cut in 4 cm pieces
green seasoning (blended culantro, thyme, garlic, scallion)

steps: Wash the goat, drain well and rub in the green seasoning, 1 tablespoon of curry powder, salt and pepper. Marinate at least 2 hours.
Mix the remaining curry powder with a little water into a thick paste.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste with the onion and garlic for 3 to 4 minutes until it darkens and smells toasted.
Add the goat and brown over high heat for 8 minutes, stirring so the curry coats every piece.
Add the water and the whole pepper, cover and simmer on low heat for 1.5 hours, adding a bit more water if needed.
Add the potatoes and cook for 25 more minutes until they are tender and the gravy is thick.
Remove the whole pepper and serve with rice, dhalpuri roti or paratha.

title: Dhalpuri roti (Trinidadian split pea-stuffed flatbread)

ingredients.name: vegetable oil, plus more for cooking

steps: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt, add the oil and water and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 1 hour.
Boil the split peas in water for 35 to 40 minutes until soft but not mushy, then drain well, dry them in a pan for a minute and grind to a coarse powder.
Mix the ground peas with the garlic, geera, turmeric, hot pepper and salt.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Flatten each ball, place 2 tablespoons of the filling in the middle, pinch the dough closed around it and flatten with your palm.
Roll each filled ball out gently into a thin round of 22 to 25 cm.
Cook on a hot dry griddle or tawa for about 1 minute, flip, brush with oil and cook until blistered and golden on both sides.
Wrap the roti in a clean cloth and clap it between your hands to loosen the layers. Serve warm with curry.

title: Doubles (Trinidadian curried chickpeas in fried flatbread)

ingredients.name: dried chickpeas, soaked overnight (or 2 cans, about 800 g, drained)
oil for frying, tamarind chutney and pepper sauce to serve

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, turmeric, cumin and salt, then stir in the warm water to make a soft, sticky dough. Cover and let it rise for 1 hour.
If using dried chickpeas, boil them in unsalted water for 45 to 60 minutes until completely tender, then drain. Canned chickpeas need no boiling.
Make a paste of the curry powder with a little water and fry it in 2 tablespoons of oil with the onion and garlic for 3 to 4 minutes until it smells toasted.
Add the chickpeas, geera, salt and 250 ml of water. Simmer for 20 minutes, mashing some of the chickpeas, until the curry is thick and saucy. Stir in the culantro.

With oiled hands, pinch off a piece of the dough about the size of a golf ball, stretch it into a thin round of about 12 cm and fry it in 3 cm of hot oil for 30 to 40 seconds per side until puffed and pale gold. These are the bara. Drain on paper towels.
To serve, place a spoonful of curried chickpeas between two warm bara and top with pepper sauce and tamarind chutney.

title: Fried bake (Trinidadian fried flour dough bread)
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt together in a bowl.
Rub in the butter until the mixture looks like breadcrumbs.
Add the warm water gradually and knead for 3 to 4 minutes into a smooth, soft dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls and roll each into a flat round about 1 cm thick.
Heat 3 cm of oil to medium-high heat and fry the rounds for about 2 minutes per side, spooning hot oil over the tops, until they puff and turn golden brown.
Drain on paper towels. Serve hot with saltfish, buljol, eggs, cheese or jam.

title: Geera pork (Trinidadian roasted cumin pork)

ingredients.name: pork shoulder, cut in 3 cm cubes

steps: Toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan until fragrant and darker, then grind them to a powder.
Toss the pork with the ground geera, garam masala, onion, garlic, scallions, culantro, thyme, hot pepper, black pepper and salt. Cover and marinate in the fridge overnight.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over high heat and fry the pork in batches for 5 minutes until it browns.
Return all the pork to the pot and add 150 ml of water. Cover and cook over low heat for 30 to 40 minutes until the pork is tender.
Uncover and cook off the remaining liquid, stirring, until the pork is coated in a dry spiced residue and lightly fried in its own fat.
Serve hot as finger food with hot pepper sauce, or with roti or rice.

title: Goat roti (Trinidadian curried goat wrap)

ingredients.name: goat meat, bone-in, cut in small pieces
green seasoning (blended culantro, thyme, garlic, scallion)

steps: Marinate the goat in the green seasoning, a tablespoon of curry powder and salt for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Mix the remaining curry powder with water into a paste and fry it in the hot oil with the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the goat and stir over high heat for 5 to 8 minutes until the meat takes up the curry and browns lightly.
Pour in the water, cover and simmer for 1 to 1.5 hours until the goat is almost tender.
Add the potatoes and chickpeas and cook for 20 more minutes, uncovered, until they are tender and the gravy has thickened.
Take the meat off the bones if you like, spoon a portion into each warm roti with plenty of gravy, add pepper sauce, fold and roll up like a burrito.

title: Macaroni pie (Trinidadian baked cheese macaroni)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and grease a 23 x 33 cm baking dish.
Boil the macaroni in well-salted water for about 8 minutes until just tender, then drain and return to the pot with the butter.
Add the onion, bell pepper, mustard and hot sauce, then stir in two thirds of the cheese.
Beat the eggs with the evaporated milk and plenty of black pepper, then stir into the macaroni.
Pour into the baking dish, top with the remaining cheese and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until set with a golden crust.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut into squares, so the pie holds together when served.

title: Mango kuchela (Trinidadian spicy green mango relish)

ingredients.name: large green (unripe) mangoes, peeled and coarsely grated (about 500 g)
mustard oil or neutral vegetable oil
amchar masala (or equal parts ground coriander, cumin, fennel, mustard seed and fenugreek)
scotch bonnet or other hot pepper, minced

steps: Toss the grated mango with the salt and leave in a colander for 30 minutes, then squeeze out as much liquid as possible with your hands.
Heat the oil in a small pan until shimmering, then take it off the heat for a minute so it is hot but not smoking.
Add the amchar masala and garlic to the oil and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to burn.
Pour the spiced oil over the mango, add the hot pepper, sugar and vinegar and mix thoroughly.
Let it mature for at least 2 hours or overnight in the fridge.
Serve as a condiment with doubles, pelau, roti or fried fish.

title: Pastelles (Trinidadian Christmas cornmeal parcels with spiced beef)

ingredients.name: green seasoning (blended culantro, thyme, garlic, scallion)
squares of banana leaf, softened over a flame (or parchment and foil)

steps: Fry the onion and garlic in a little oil for 3 minutes, then add the beef, green seasoning, salt and pepper and brown it for 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, brown sugar and 100 ml of water and cook down until almost dry, then mix in the raisins, olives and capers. Let it cool.
Mix the cornmeal, butter and 1 teaspoon of salt, then add the hot water gradually and knead to a soft, smooth dough that is not sticky.
Place a banana leaf square or parchment on the counter, grease it and spread a golf-ball-sized portion of dough into a thin 10 cm round.
Put 2 tablespoons of filling in the middle, fold the leaf so the dough encloses the filling and make a flat package, then tie with string.
Steam the pastelles in a pot with a rack and a little water for about 1 hour, until the dough is firm and peels away from the leaf.
Unwrap and serve warm, a Christmas speciality.

title: Peanut punch (Trinidadian peanut butter milk drink)
steps: Put the peanut butter and a splash of the milk in a blender and blend until smooth, to prevent clumps.
Add the rest of the milk, condensed milk, sugar, nutmeg, cinnamon, vanilla and bitters, if using.
Blend on high for 1 minute until frothy and completely smooth.
Taste and add more sugar if needed.
Pour over ice in tall glasses and serve very cold, with a little extra nutmeg on top.

title: Pelau (Trinidadian caramelised chicken and pigeon pea rice)

ingredients.name: green seasoning (blended culantro, thyme, garlic, scallion, pepper)

steps: Season the chicken with the green seasoning, salt and pepper and leave to marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat, add the sugar and let it bubble until dark amber and smoking slightly.
Add the chicken and turn it to coat it in the caramel, browning it well for 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the onion, bell pepper and carrots and cook for 3 minutes, then stir in the ketchup.
Add the rice, pigeon peas, coconut milk, stock, butter and whole pepper, and stir well. Bring to a boil.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 25 to 30 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes, remove the whole pepper, fluff and serve with coleslaw, salad or fried plantain.

title: Pholourie (Trinidadian split pea fritters with tamarind chutney)

ingredients.name: yellow split pea flour (or yellow split peas ground fine)
oil for frying, tamarind chutney to serve

steps: Whisk the split pea flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, yeast, turmeric, geera and salt in a bowl.
Stir in the garlic, culantro and hot pepper, then add the warm water gradually, beating to a thick, smooth batter that drops from the spoon.
Cover and let the batter rest for 1 hour until it has risen and is bubbly.
Heat 5 cm of oil to about 175 C.
Drop teaspoon-sized portions of batter into the oil, in batches, and fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden and puffed into round balls.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with tamarind chutney for dipping.

title: Saheena (Trinidadian dasheen leaf and split pea fritters)

ingredients.name: young dasheen (taro) leaves, or spinach, finely chopped
yellow split pea flour (or ground split peas)
oil for frying, tamarind chutney to serve

steps: Wash the leaves well and chop them finely, discarding thick stems. If using taro, make sure the pieces are very small, since they must be fully cooked.
Mix the split pea flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, turmeric, geera and salt, then stir in the water to make a thick batter.
Fold the chopped leaves, onion, garlic and culantro into the batter until evenly mixed.
Heat 3 cm of oil to medium heat.
Spoon the mixture in tablespoon-sized portions into the oil, flattening slightly, and fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with tamarind or mango chutney.

title: Trinidadian chicken curry (green-seasoned curry chicken)

ingredients.name: green seasoning (blended culantro, thyme, garlic, scallion, peppers)
potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks

steps: Season the chicken with the green seasoning, salt and pepper and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Mix the curry powder with a few tablespoons of water into a paste.

Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat, add the paste and cook it for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and smells toasted. This step, called burning the curry, gives the dish its flavour.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 2 minutes, then add the chicken and stir over high heat for 8 minutes until it is coated and lightly browned.
Add the water and whole pepper, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook 20 more minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy thick. Remove the pepper and serve with roti, rice or bread.
